entities.name: MHT skin meta-analysis
observations: A 2023 meta-analysis of 15 clinical studies involving 1,589 women found higher skin elasticity, thickness, and collagen with oral or transdermal menopausal hormone therapy, but no significant effect on dryness; authors called for better-conducted trials.

entities.name: Systemic estrogen RCT
observations: In a small double-blind placebo-controlled trial of 41 postmenopausal women, six months of cyclic oral estradiol valerate plus cyproterone acetate increased upper-arm biopsy collagen by 6.49%; epidermal/keratin measures and elastic fibers did not significantly change.

entities.name: HRT skin evidence limitations
observations: Reviews describe favorable collagen, dermal thickness, and elasticity findings but discordant results for elastin, sebum, wrinkling, blood flow, and other outcomes; large clinical trials are needed.

entities.name: Low-dose systemic estrogen uncertainty
observations: A 2021 dermatology review reported that a later rigorous study found low-dose systemic estrogen did not overcome effects of actinic exposure, smoking, racial makeup, or aging, and characterized current low-dose systemic hormone effects as not well established.

entities.name: Topical estrogen not systemic evidence
observations: A 2007 pilot adding topical facial estradiol to women already receiving systemic estrogen reported increased epithelial/dermal thickness and collagen, but it did not isolate an independent systemic effect.
